items.topic: Cold therapy — wrap ice in cloth; do not place ice directly on skin
items.stem: The nurse teaches a client to use an ice pack for a soft-tissue injury. Which instruction is correct?

options.text: Wrap the ice in a cloth and apply it; do not place ice directly on the skin
Place bare ice cubes directly against the skin for continuous 2-hour contact
Apply uncovered dry ice directly over open abrasions
Heat the ice pack in a microwave before applying it to the skin

rationales.A: Correct. MedlinePlus: wrap ice in cloth; do not place ice directly on the skin. Merck: apply ice wrapped in a towel or cloth.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Direct ice and prolonged unprotected cold risk skin injury.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Ice should not be placed directly on skin; open skin needs separate wound care.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Ice packs are used cold; heating defeats cold therapy and risks burn.

items.topic: NGN matrix — cold pack safety teaching indicated vs not
items.stem: For safe home use of an ice pack on a sprain, indicate whether each teaching point is Indicated or Not indicated.

rows.text: Wrap the ice pack in a cloth before applying to skin
Limit applications to about 15–20 minutes at a time as taught
Place bare ice directly on unprotected skin for continuous hours
Reassess skin for excessive redness, blistering, or numbness

rationales.R1: Indicated. MedlinePlus/Merck: wrap ice in cloth/towel before applying.
rationales.R2: Indicated. MedlinePlus elbow aftercare: ice 15–20 minutes at a time.
rationales.R3: Not indicated. Direct ice on skin is unsafe; wrap in cloth/towel.
rationales.R4: Indicated. Protecting skin from cold injury requires monitoring the site.

items.topic: Bed-to-wheelchair transfer — lock wheelchair brakes before transfer
items.stem: The nurse prepares to assist a partially weight-bearing client from bed to a wheelchair. Which action is essential before the transfer?

options.text: Lock the wheelchair brakes and stabilize the chair; clear footrests/leg rests as needed
Leave the wheelchair unlocked so it can roll toward the client
Ask the client to hold the moving wheelchair while standing unsupported
Place the wheelchair at the far end of the room without locking it

rationales.A: Correct. MyHealth Alberta: prepare the wheelchair by locking the brakes and removing/swinging away leg rests. OpenStax: before transfer, lock and stabilize equipment.
rationales.B: Incorrect. An unlocked wheelchair can roll and cause a fall.
rationales.C: Incorrect. The chair must be locked/stabilized; the client should not stabilize a moving chair.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Chair should be positioned close and locked.

items.topic: NGN matrix — bed-to-wheelchair transfer safety actions
items.stem: Before assisting a client from bed to wheelchair, indicate whether each action is Indicated or Not indicated.

rows.text: Remove or swing away leg rests that could trip the client
Leave brakes unlocked so the chair rolls with the pivot
Use a transfer/gait belt when additional secure hold is needed

rationales.R1: Indicated. Alberta: lock the brakes. OpenStax: lock and stabilize equipment.
rationales.R2: Indicated. Alberta: remove or swing away both leg rests.
rationales.R3: Not indicated. Unlocked wheels increase fall risk during transfer.
rationales.R4: Indicated. Alberta and OpenStax support transfer/gait belt use for safer assistance.

items.topic: SSI prevention — avoid hair removal unless necessary; clippers not razors
items.client_needs_subcategory: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
items.stem: A preoperative nurse prepares the surgical site. Which hair-removal practice best aligns with SSI prevention guidance?

options.text: Do not remove hair unless it will interfere with the operation; if removal is needed, use clippers (not a razor)
Shave the entire surgical field with a razor the night before surgery
Always remove all hair at every incision site with a disposable razor in the OR
Use a razor immediately before incision because microscopic cuts reduce infection

rationales.A: Correct. SHEA: do not remove hair unless it interferes; if needed, clip outside the OR; do not use razors. ACS/SIS: avoid hair removal unless hair interferes; if needed use clippers instead of a razor.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Routine razor shaving increases SSI risk.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Routine removal is discouraged; razors are not preferred.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Razor microtrauma is linked to higher SSI risk.

items.topic: C. difficile — environmental cleaning with sporicidal agent
items.client_needs_subcategory: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
items.stem: Environmental services asks which product to use for daily cleaning of a room occupied by a client with Clostridioides difficile infection. Which response is best?

options.text: Use a C. difficile sporicidal disinfectant (for example, an EPA List K agent) for daily and terminal cleaning
Wipe surfaces with plain water only; spores are removed by rinsing
Use alcohol wipes alone as the primary room disinfectant for C. difficile spores
Skip terminal cleaning after discharge because spores die within minutes on dry surfaces

rationales.A: Correct. CDC CDI guidance: daily and terminal cleaning with a C. difficile sporicidal agent (EPA List K). Public Health Ontario: use a sporicidal agent for CDI bathroom cleaning and for discharge/transfer cleaning of the room/bathroom.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Cleaning alone without a sporicidal disinfectant is inadequate for CDI rooms.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Alcohol is not relied on as a sporicidal agent for C. difficile environmental disinfection.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Terminal cleaning with a sporicidal agent after transfer/discharge is recommended.

sources.title: Clinical Guidance for C. diff Infection Prevention in Acute Care Facilities
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.evidence: Daily/terminal cleaning with C. difficile sporicidal agent (EPA List K).

sources.title: Significant Organisms in Environmental Cleaning — FAQs
sources.evidence: Use sporicidal agent for CDI bathroom/room cleaning and discharge/transfer cleaning.

items.topic: Facility fire response — RACE: Rescue, Alarm, Confine/Contain, Extinguish
items.client_needs_subcategory: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
items.stem: A nurse discovers a small wastebasket fire in an unoccupied patient room. Which response sequence best reflects standard healthcare fire response (RACE)?

options.text: Rescue anyone in immediate danger, activate the alarm, confine/contain the fire (close doors), then extinguish if safe
Ignore the alarm pull stations and first search for an elevator to evacuate the whole building
Open all doors on the unit to improve airflow before calling for help
Leave clients in the fire room while gathering personal belongings from the nursing station

rationales.A: Correct. NCBI/StatPearls (OSHA fire safety): RACE = rescue, alarm, confine, extinguish. Ohio healthcare fire tip sheet: Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Extinguish — rescue persons in immediate danger.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Elevators are not used for fire evacuation; alarm activation is required.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Confinement requires closing doors, not opening them to feed the fire.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Rescue of those in danger and alarm/confine take priority over retrieving belongings.

sources.title: OSHA Fire Safety
sources.evidence: RACE = rescue, alarm, confine, extinguish.

sources.publisher: Ohio Department of Commerce — Division of State Fire Marshal

items.topic: Tardive dyskinesia — involuntary orofacial movements; assess/report (AIMS)
items.stem: A client on long-term antipsychotic therapy develops involuntary lip smacking and tongue protrusion. Which nursing interpretation and action are most appropriate?

options.text: Suspect tardive dyskinesia; assess with an involuntary-movement tool (e.g., AIMS) and notify the provider
Reassure that these movements always resolve within minutes and require no follow-up
Immediately double the antipsychotic dose without notifying the provider
Interpret the movements as voluntary attention-seeking and ignore them

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: tardive dyskinesia presents with involuntary facial movements (lip smacking, tongue protruding); use AIMS to assess EPS/TD. Merck: TD involves involuntary lip/tongue movements; patients on long-term therapy should be evaluated periodically with AIMS.
rationales.B: Incorrect. TD may persist and needs assessment/provider notification.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Dose increases are not an independent nursing action and may worsen EPS/TD risk.
rationales.D: Incorrect. TD movements are involuntary adverse effects, not voluntary behaviour.

items.topic: NGN matrix — suspected tardive dyskinesia nursing actions
items.stem: A client on chronic antipsychotic therapy has new involuntary tongue and lip movements. Indicate whether each nursing action is Indicated or Not indicated.

rows.text: Perform/assist with an Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale (AIMS) assessment
Notify the provider/prescriber of the new involuntary movements
Document the findings and continue scheduled monitoring
Tell the client the movements are intentional and withhold reporting

rationales.R2: Indicated. New TD signs require clinician notification for regimen review.
rationales.R3: Indicated. Ongoing evaluation/documentation is part of safe long-term antipsychotic care.
rationales.R4: Not indicated. TD movements are involuntary adverse effects and must not be dismissed.

items.topic: NGN bowtie — command auditory hallucinations: prioritize safety assessment
items.stem: A client with schizophrenia reports voices telling them to harm themselves. Complete the bowtie: most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.

conditions.text: Command auditory hallucinations with elevated self-harm risk
Resolved medication adherence with no safety concerns

actions.text: Assess suicide/violence risk and ensure immediate environmental safety
Stay with the client / increase observation per protocol while notifying the team
Argue that the voices are impossible and leave the client alone in a room with sharps
Ignore the report because hallucinations are always harmless
Encourage the client to act on the commands to 'test reality'

parameters.text: Presence/content of command hallucinations and intent to act
Level of observation / access to means of harm

rationales.K1: Correct. OpenStax: command auditory hallucinations direct the person to do things such as violence toward self or others.
rationales.K2: Incorrect. Grief alone does not explain command hallucinations.
rationales.K4: Incorrect. Command hallucinations indicate ongoing safety concern.
rationales.A1: Correct. OpenStax: safety is paramount; assess suicide and violence risk.
rationales.A2: Correct. Maintaining safety/observation and team notification are priority actions.
rationales.A3: Incorrect. Arguing and leaving with means available increase harm risk.
rationales.A4: Incorrect. Command hallucinations are not harmless.
rationales.A5: Incorrect. Never encourage acting on harmful commands.
rationales.P1: Correct. Monitor hallucination content and intent to act.
rationales.P2: Correct. Observation level and means restriction are key safety parameters.
rationales.P3: Incorrect. Not a safety parameter for command hallucinations.

items.topic: Akathisia — motor restlessness from antipsychotics; report; do not ignore
items.stem: Two days after starting a first-generation antipsychotic, a client paces constantly and says, “I feel like I can’t sit still.” Which nursing conclusion is best?

options.text: This may be akathisia (motor restlessness); assess and notify the provider because it is distressing and can lead to nonadherence
This is always intentional hyperactivity and should be ignored
This proves the client needs a higher antipsychotic dose immediately without assessment
This is pathognomonic of tardive dyskinesia lip-smacking that requires no reporting

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: akathisia includes restlessness and inability to sit still, often early after starting/increasing dose. Merck: akathisia (motor restlessness) is particularly unpleasant and may lead to nonadherence.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Akathisia is an adverse effect, not willful behaviour.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Dose increases without assessment may worsen EPS; notify provider.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Classic TD is late orofacial involuntary movements, not acute restlessness.

items.jurisdiction_note: CNO Documentation practice standard (in effect Feb 1, 2026) is Ontario regulatory authority for nursing documentation accountabilities.
items.topic: CNO Documentation — timely entries; do not document before care is provided
items.stem: An Ontario RN is charting after a busy morning. Which action meets CNO Documentation accountabilities?

options.text: Document care in a timely manner at the time of care or as soon as possible afterward — and do not document care before it is provided
Pre-chart anticipated care for the entire shift before assessing any clients
Delete another nurse’s entry that the RN disagrees with
Falsify a late vital-sign entry to match expected values

rationales.A: Correct. CNO Documentation: document in a timely manner at the time of care or as soon as possible after; nurses do not document before the care is provided.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Documenting before care is provided is prohibited.
rationales.C: Incorrect. CNO: do not delete, alter, or modify documentation produced by others.
rationales.D: Incorrect. CNO: do not falsify a record relating to practice.

sources.title: Documentation
sources.evidence: Document timely; do not document before care; do not falsify; do not alter others’ entries.

sources.section: Principles of the Code / professional accountability
